raw.title: UNESCO Communication and Information Sector Internship
raw.description: Unpaid internship of 1 to 6 months with UNESCO's Communication and Information Sector at Headquarters, field offices or institutes. Interns support programme and project work, research and knowledge products, partnerships and operations on freedom of expression, media and information literacy, access to information and digital transformation. Applying places you in a pool of intern candidates rather than for one specific post. Hiring managers pick from the pool, and a candidature stays valid for six months. UNESCO pays interns nothing. Interns arrange and fund their own travel, visa and health insurance.
raw.location: UNESCO Headquarters (Paris), field offices and institutes

additionalRequirements: Currently enrolled in the third or final year of a bachelor's degree, OR enrolled in a second university degree, master's or PhD, OR completed a bachelor's, master's or PhD no more than 12 months before the internship agreement is issued.
Technical or vocational applicants must be in their last year at a specialised institution or have graduated within the last 12 months.
Excellent written and spoken English or French.

raw.applicationInstructions: Apply through the UNESCO careers portal. Have your CV and motivation letter ready. The application must be finished within one hour, in English or French.

raw.title: Heinz Heinen Fellowships 2027/2028
raw.organizationName: Bonn Center for Dependency and Slavery Studies (BCDSS), University of Bonn
raw.description: Research fellowships at the University of Bonn's Cluster of Excellence on dependency and slavery studies for the 2027/2028 academic year. They are open to doctoral fellows about to finish a PhD (up to 6 months), junior postdocs (PhD within four years, up to 12 months), postdocs (up to 12 months), senior fellows (up to 6 months) and alternative knowledge producers such as journalists, artists and curators (up to 6 months). Research should be historical, focused on the period before 1900, and comparative. Monthly stipends run from €1,700 for doctoral fellows to €3,600 for senior fellows. Fellows also receive a travel allowance, an accommodation lump sum of up to €1,000 a month for those from outside Bonn, and workspace. The earliest start date is 1 October 2027.

additionalRequirements: Doctoral, postdoctoral or senior scholars, or alternative knowledge producers.
Research proposal on historical research in Slavery and Dependency Studies, focused on the period before 1900.
Application documents in English, combined into one PDF, with two letters of recommendation sent directly by referees (depending on category).

raw.title: Atlantic Fellows for Social and Economic Equity (AFSEE) 2027-28 Cohort
raw.organizationName: Atlantic Fellows for Social and Economic Equity, LSE International Inequalities Institute
raw.description: A funded fellowship based at the LSE International Inequalities Institute for people working to challenge inequalities. There is a Residential track, which also requires admission to the MSc in Inequalities and Social Science at LSE, and a Non-Residential track. Applicants need at least 7 years of experience and must meet LSE's English language requirements. The programme says most of its Fellows come from the Global South and that it is especially keen to support applicants who live there. Applications go through LSE's graduate application system with two references, transcripts, a statement of academic purpose and a CV. Decisions are expected by mid-April 2027.
raw.location: London, United Kingdom (Residential track); Non-Residential track also offered

additionalRequirements: Meet LSE's English Language Requirements.
Residential track applicants must also qualify for admission to the MSc in Inequalities and Social Science at LSE.
Two referees must submit references by the reference deadline.

raw.title: Rufford Small Grants for Nature Conservation
raw.description: Staged grants from The Rufford Foundation for nature conservation projects in emerging and developing economies. There are four levels of support: a 1st and 2nd Rufford Small Grant, a Booster Grant and a Completion Grant. Grants range from £7,000 to £18,000. The funder focuses on people early in a conservation career, mainly current MSc or PhD students and recent graduates, and does not fund undergraduates. The project must have a nature conservation focus, be in an eligible country, and work on species considered threatened. Applications are accepted all year, and unsuccessful applicants can re-apply after 12 months.
raw.location: Project must be in an eligible country (Uganda is on the eligible list)

additionalRequirements: Early stage of a conservation career; mainly current MSc or PhD students or recent graduates, though others can apply if they meet the additional criteria. Undergraduate students are not funded.
Project must have a nature conservation focus.
Project must be in an eligible country.
Any species worked on must be considered threatened.
Unsuccessful applicants may re-apply after 12 months.

raw.title: Uganda Regional Data Coordinator (Fixed-term), One Acre Fund
raw.description: Two-year fixed-term role (renewable) based in Mubende with One Acre Fund's Uganda programme. The coordinator leads regional data processes, sets up and manages digital survey tools such as CommCare, SurveyCTO and Kobo, cleans and analyses field datasets in Excel, coordinates R&D field trials, and trains and mentors regional teams and field staff on survey design and data quality. The role needs a bachelor's degree in a quantitative field and at least two years of hands-on data experience. Benefits listed are health insurance and paid time off.

additionalRequirements: Bachelor's degree in Statistics, Data Analytics, Applied Mathematics, Quantitative Economics or a related field.
Only open to citizens or permanent residents of Uganda.

raw.title: African Union Commission Internship Program
raw.description: Full-time internship at the African Union Commission in Addis Ababa, open to nationals of AU member states. Interns give administrative and technical support across AU departments and directorates, including agriculture, trade and industry, education and technology, infrastructure and energy, peace and security, health and social development, and communications. The internship is authorised once for three months and can be renewed once. The AU has no financial obligation to interns, who cover their own travel, accommodation, living costs and insurance. Prior work experience is not required.
requiredSkills: fluency in an AU working language

additionalRequirements: Nationals of an African Union member state.
Enrolled in at least the final year of a bachelor's degree, or already holding a bachelor's or master's degree in a related field.
Fluent in at least one AU working language (Arabic, English, French or Portuguese).
No more than 32 years old at the time of selection.
No conviction for a serious criminal offence.

raw.applicationInstructions: Apply online through the AU careers portal using the mandatory AU CV template. Upload a motivation letter, passport or national ID copy, certified academic certificates, a CV and a recommendation letter from your institution.
